lead: Gravity is a weak force for separating two liquids whose densities differ by only 100 or 200 kg/m³, so plain columns are tall and mixer-settlers are large. Three ways round this are taught together. A pulsed column adds an oscillating motion to the liquid so the drops become small without moving internals. A centrifugal extractor replaces g by a centrifugal field thousands of times stronger, so contact and separation take seconds. Supercritical extraction replaces the liquid solvent by a fluid such as carbon dioxide above its critical point, whose solvent power is set by pressure and which leaves no residue. The stage and leaching balances of this unit still apply to all three.
prereq: You need Extraction equipment (Stokes settling, flooding, hold-up).

blocks.text: A pulsed column is a sieve-plate or packed column whose liquid contents are moved up and down by a piston, bellows or compressed-air pulser connected to the bottom. The plates do not move; the liquid is forced through the holes in both directions, which shears the drops small and renews their surfaces. The operating variable is the pulse intensity, the product A·f of the stroke A (the total, peak-to-peak displacement of the liquid in the column) and the frequency f. Over one cycle the liquid moves A up and A down, so its mean speed is 2Af.

At low intensity the drops are large and the column behaves like an unpulsed sieve-tray column (the mixer-settler regime, drops coalescing under each plate). As intensity rises the drops become fine and uniform (the dispersion regime), hold-up and area rise and the height of a transfer unit falls. Too much intensity makes an emulsion, and the column floods at a lower throughput. There are no seals or bearings inside the column, so pulsed columns are used where the liquid is radioactive or corrosive, as in nuclear fuel reprocessing with tributyl phosphate.
u<sub>c</sub> = Δρ d² ω² r/(18 μ<sub>c</sub>);   u<sub>c</sub>/u<sub>t</sub> = ω²r/g
blocks.where: Stokes settling in a centrifugal field: ω is the angular speed (rad/s, = 2πN/60 for N rpm), r the radius of the drop's path (m); the other symbols are as in gravity settling. ω²r/g is the number of g of the field.

blocks.text: The Podbielniak extractor is a horizontal drum spinning at a few thousand rpm, containing a long spiral (or concentric perforated cylinders). The heavy liquid enters near the shaft and is thrown outward; the light liquid enters at the rim and is forced inward; they pass counter-currently through the perforations, giving several stages in one machine. Annular centrifugal contactors mix the liquids in the gap between a spinning rotor and the casing and separate them inside the rotor, one stage per unit. Residence times are seconds and hold-up is very small, which suits penicillin (unstable at the low pH of extraction), other antibiotics and radioactive liquors. The costs are a high price, seals and maintenance. The centrifuge changes the speed of separation, not the equilibrium: stages are still counted with tie lines or the Kremser equation.

Above its critical temperature and pressure a substance is a supercritical fluid: no liquid–vapour boundary exists, the density can be liquid-like while the viscosity and diffusivity stay gas-like. Carbon dioxide is the usual choice: critical point 31.0 °C and 73.8 bar, non-toxic, non-flammable, cheap and easy to remove from the product. Near the critical point a small rise in pressure gives a large rise in density, and solvent power rises with density. At 40 °C and 200 bar CO<sub>2</sub> is about 0.84 g/cm³.

items: Compressed CO<sub>2</sub> is heated to the extraction temperature and passed through a vessel packed with the ground solid (coffee beans, hops, spices).
The solute dissolves; the loaded fluid leaves the extractor.
A pressure-reduction valve drops the pressure in a separator; the density and solvent power fall and the extract drops out.
The lean CO<sub>2</sub> is recompressed (or condensed and pumped) and recycled.

blocks.text: Pure CO<sub>2</sub> is a weak, non-polar solvent: it dissolves oils, essential oils and other low-polarity compounds well. Caffeine is moderately polar, so decaffeination uses CO<sub>2</sub> at high density, with moist beans (water helps release the caffeine), and a polar co-solvent such as a few per cent of ethanol is added when more polar solutes are wanted. The solid feed is a leaching problem, so its balances are those of leaching; only the solvent is unusual. Against conventional solvents it gives solvent-free products and low temperatures for flavours, at the price of high-pressure equipment.

examples.question: Water drops of 100 µm settle through an organic liquid (Δρ = 200 kg/m³, μ<sub>c</sub> = 1.0 mPa·s). Find the settling velocity under gravity and in a centrifugal extractor turning at 3000 rpm at r = 0.20 m. How long does each take to cross 0.30 m of a gravity settler and 10 mm of the rotor?
steps: Centrifugal: u<sub>c</sub> = 2012 × 1.09 × 10⁻³ = 2.19 m/s (Stokes' law is only a rough guide at this speed).
Times: gravity 0.30/1.09 × 10⁻³ = 275 s, about 4.6 min; centrifuge 0.010/2.19 = 0.0046 s.
examples.answer: 1.09 mm/s under gravity against about 2.2 m/s at 2012 g; separation drops from minutes to milliseconds.

examples.question: 2.0 kg of ground spice holding 5 mass% essential oil is extracted with CO<sub>2</sub> at 40 °C and 200 bar. The fluid leaving the bed holds 1.5 mass% oil, taken as its saturation loading at these conditions. Find the CO<sub>2</sub> needed to remove all the oil and the time at 5 kg/h of CO<sub>2</sub>.
steps: Leaving fluid: 0.015 kg oil per kg of oil-plus-CO<sub>2</sub>, so 0.100 kg oil needs 0.100/0.015 = 6.67 kg of solution.
CO<sub>2</sub> = 6.67 − 0.100 = 6.57 kg. This is a minimum: it assumes the fluid leaves saturated all the time, which holds only while easily reached oil remains.
examples.answer: At least 6.57 kg of CO<sub>2</sub>, about 1.31 h at 5 kg/h; in practice the end of the run is diffusion-limited and takes longer.

traps: Check how the stroke is defined: pulse intensity A·f uses the peak-to-peak stroke; with an amplitude a measured from the mean, the stroke is 2a.
A centrifuge speeds settling; it does not change the tie lines or the number of ideal stages.
Supercritical CO<sub>2</sub> is not a gas without solvent power: at 200 bar it is about as dense as a liquid, and its solvent power is adjusted with pressure.
In the CO<sub>2</sub> balance use the oil fraction of the leaving fluid (0.015), not that of the feed solid (0.05), and remember 1.5 mass% means per kg of solution, not per kg of CO<sub>2</sub>.
Saying CO<sub>2</sub> removes caffeine because caffeine is non-polar is wrong; caffeine is moderately polar and the process relies on dense CO<sub>2</sub> and moisture.

quiz.q: State the critical temperature and pressure of CO<sub>2</sub>.
Name two types of centrifugal extractor.
quiz.a: The Podbielniak extractor and the annular centrifugal contactor.

quiz.q: Why does moderate pulsing reduce the height of an extraction column?
quiz.a: Pulsing forces the liquid through the plate holes both ways, making small drops with fresh surfaces; area per volume and the mass transfer coefficient rise, so the height of a transfer unit falls.

quiz.q: How is the extract recovered from supercritical CO<sub>2</sub>?
quiz.a: The pressure is reduced (or the temperature changed) in a separator; the fluid's density and solvent power fall, the solute drops out, and the lean CO<sub>2</sub> is recompressed and recycled.

quiz.q: A pulsed column has a stroke of 12 mm and runs at 1.2 Hz. Find the pulse intensity and the mean liquid speed.
5 kg of spice holds 8 mass% oil and the CO<sub>2</sub> leaves at 2.0 mass% oil. Find the minimum CO<sub>2</sub>.
quiz.a: Oil 0.40 kg; solution 0.40/0.02 = 20.0 kg; CO<sub>2</sub> 19.6 kg.

quiz.q: A plant extracts an antibiotic that decomposes within minutes at the extraction pH. Mixer-settler or centrifugal extractor? Give two reasons.
quiz.a: Centrifugal: contact and separation take seconds, so little product decomposes, and the small hold-up keeps the inventory of product and solvent low. A mixer-settler holds the liquid for minutes in the mixer and settler.

beyond: Not for the exam. Pulsed columns remain the workhorse of nuclear fuel reprocessing; annular centrifugal contactors are used for the same duty and for rare-earth separation. Supercritical CO<sub>2</sub> plants decaffeinate coffee and tea and extract hops, spices and botanical oils; research looks at co-solvents, high-pressure mass transfer and the energy of recompression. Search for pulsed sieve-plate column, Podbielniak extractor and supercritical CO<sub>2</sub> decaffeination.

figure.caption: The supercritical CO₂ loop of the second worked example. Dense CO₂ at 40 °C and 200 bar dissolves the oil in the extractor; dropping the pressure in the separator makes the oil fall out, and the lean CO₂ is recompressed. At 1.5 % oil in the leaving fluid, 0.10 kg of oil needs at least 6.57 kg of CO₂.
